stops.title: 12 Principles of Green Chemistry & Atom economy
stops.inShort: Green chemistry minimizes waste and hazardous substances. Atom economy = (Formula weight of desired product / Sum of formula weights of all reactants) × 100%. Ozone layer depletion involves NO/CFCs.

stops.title: Nanochemistry, nanostructures, synthesis & applications
stops.inShort: Nanomaterials have 1–100 nm dimensions. 0D (nanoparticles), 1D (nanorods, nanotubes, nanowires), 2D (nanofilms). Sol-gel process involves hydrolysis of metal alkoxides: M(OR)_n + H₂O → M(OR)_{n−1}(OH) + ROH. Silver nanoparticles remove E. coli from water.

items.f: % Atom economy = (FW of desired product / ∑ FW of reactants) × 100

board.answer: (a) NO (nitric oxide reacts catalytically with ozone: NO + O₃ → NO₂ + O₂).

board.text: One dimensional nanostructure amongst the following is ____.
board.answer: (b) Nanotubes (or nanorods/nanowires — two dimensions are in nanoscale, one is outside).

board.text: What is atom economy? Explain any two applications of nanomaterials.
board.answer:
Atom economy is a measure of the amount of atoms from the starting materials that are present in the useful products at the end of a chemical process: % Atom economy = (Formula weight of desired product / Sum of formula weights of all reactants) × 100.
Applications of nanomaterials:
1. Water purification: Silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) kill E. coli bacteria.
2. Medicine: Targeted drug delivery and sunscreens (ZnO/TiO₂ nanoparticles).

points.text: Definition and formula of atom economy

board.text: Write the name of metal nanoparticle used to remove E.coli bacteria from water.
What is nano material? Write the reaction involved in sol-gel process during hydrolysis.
board.answer:
Nanomaterial: A material having structural components with at least one dimension in the nanometer scale (1–100 nm).
Hydrolysis in sol-gel process:
M−OR + H₂O → M−OH + R−OH (e.g., Si(OC₂H₅)₄ + H₂O → Si(OC₂H₅)₃OH + C₂H₅OH).
